q: How does the choice of V^h vs V^h_0 for the codomain of the discrete Laplacian -Δ_h (Eq. 5.1) affect convergence in practice? The paper writes '-Δ_h : H^1_0 → V^h' without disambiguating boundary dofs.
basis: We initially implemented -Δ_h with test functions in the full V^h (i.e. including boundary dofs), then took M^{-1}A u_c as the resulting coefficients. This produced ~O(1/h) contamination at boundary nodes and yielded convergence rates ~0.3-0.5 instead of the theoretical O(h). Switching to test functions in V^h_0 (interior only) with z_boundary := 0 recovered the exact theoretical O(h) H^1-velocity rate and machine-precision reproduction of P1 polynomials.
next_steps: Add a boxed implementation remark to any tutorial/textbook exposition of the method; run a controlled experiment computing ||-Δ_h u||_L∞ vs h for the two choices to quantify the O(1/h) contamination; check whether existing implementations in FEniCS/Firedrake/deal.II tutorials get this right.

q: Does the new Bochev-Gunzburger discrete SGLS method produce better-conditioned linear systems than the classical Hughes-Franca-Balestra (1986) pressure-Poisson method on high-aspect-ratio or high-Reynolds-number meshes, as conjectured in Section 6?
basis: Sec. 6 speculates 'Compared with the absolutely stable RGLS methods, the new formulation avoids the appearance of local biharmonic terms that in principle should lead to better conditioned matrices,' but no measurement is provided. Our implementation makes such a study easy: assemble both matrices, compute κ_2 via ARPACK, sweep aspect ratio.
next_steps: Sweep 2D mesh anisotropy from 1:1 to 1:100; report κ(K) for (a) B-G SGLS with -Δ_h, (b) standard PSPG (no -Δ_h term), (c) RGLS (α=-1). Compare GMRES iteration counts for each with identity preconditioning.

q: What is the optimal δ as a function of h, mesh geometry, and problem data, and does it follow a predictable scaling like δ_opt = C·h^p·ν^q?
basis: Our absolute-stability sweep (Table 4.3) shows ‖p-pʰ‖_L² varies non-monotonically with δ over 10⁻⁶..10⁴; the minimum sits near δ≈1 for our Taylor-Green + P1/P1 case at h≈0.09. Theorem 5.4 gives no operational recipe (the constant C(δ) is not characterized). A user picking δ 'blindly' can be a decade or two off optimal.
next_steps: Grid-search δ for each h over 5 orders of magnitude; extract δ_opt(h); fit power law; compare with published SUPG/PSPG heuristics (δ ~ h²/ν). Repeat for varying viscosity to test the h/ν scaling.

q: Does the absolute-stability proof of Theorem 5.4 extend to the Oseen problem (linearized Navier-Stokes with a given advection field) with a convective SUPG stabilization added to the residual?
basis: The paper is Stokes-only. Real-world CFD is Navier-Stokes; the standard PSPG framework of Hughes/Franca extends naturally by including (u·∇u - Δu + ∇p - f) in the residual with a SUPG-like weight. Whether the -Δ_h substitution + weak-consistency argument of Lemma 5.2 still gives absolute stability is not obvious — the advection introduces a first-order operator that changes the coercivity structure.
next_steps: Implement Oseen (steady) with a fixed advection β; try both the SUPG-Bochev-Gunzburger hybrid and pure PSPG; sweep δ; check if absolute stability persists across a range of Peclet numbers Pe = |β|h/ν.

q: Can the method be extended to discontinuous-pressure spaces (e.g. P1_disc, P0), and does absolute stability persist?
basis: The paper explicitly requires continuous pressure (∇pʰ ∈ L²(Ω)) so that the (∇pʰ, ∇qʰ)_0 stabilization term is well-defined element-wise. Sec. 6 last paragraph: 'Extending our results to discontinuous pressure spaces would also be valuable.' For DG pressures the natural analogue would add face-jump terms with a suitable interior-penalty structure.
next_steps: Design a hybrid H(div)/DG-pressure variant using (∇_h pʰ, ∇_h qʰ)_element + η/h⟨[[pʰ]], [[qʰ]]⟩_face; run the same absolute-stability sweep on lowest-order Raviart-Thomas velocity + P0 pressure; compare with Cockburn-Kanschat-Schötzau HDG methods that already handle equal-order without stabilization.
